must_remember: The Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics states that if system A is in thermal equilibrium with system C, and system B is also in thermal equilibrium with system C, then A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
A diathermic wall allows heat exchange between systems, whereas an adiabatic wall is an insulating boundary preventing heat transfer.
Temperature is an intensive scalar property representing the macroscopic manifestation of average translational kinetic energy per molecule ($E_k = \frac{3}{2} k_B T$).
Thermal equilibrium is achieved when macroscopic properties such as pressure, volume, and electrical resistance cease to change with time.
The absolute temperature scale defines the triple point of water precisely at $273.16\text{ K}$.

glossary.meaning: A conducting boundary that permits systems to exchange energy in the form of heat.
An insulating boundary that prevents any heat transfer between systems in contact.
A state in which two or more systems in thermal contact experience no net heat flow and have identical temperatures.
The principle establishing the transitivity of thermal equilibrium, forming the foundational basis for temperature measurement.
A measurable physical property of a substance that varies monotonically with temperature, used to construct temperature scales.
